correctness.rationale: For every odd m>=3, the graph incidence vectors span the (2m-1)-dimensional zero-sum tangent space; rim and spoke centered covariances share the same barycenter. Fourier plus/minus modes give exactly 2m-1 strictly positive eigenvalues. Root-of-unity products yield determinant F_m(u)^2 (1-u^2)^m/(2m)^(2m-1). Strict logdet concavity in x and positive derivative m(m-2) at zero ensure the unique interior maximizing x=u^2. Its derivative makes both vertex orbit leverage values equal dimension d, so the weighted contact moment criterion proves global Löwner optimality, not merely symmetric-stationarity. The implicit equation implies u<1/2 and x=1/4-3^(-m)+O(m9^(-m)). Recomputed matrix, eigenvalue, determinant and contact equalities independently in the package checker for odd m=3..19; finite checks are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The minimum enclosing ellipsoid is a canonical intrinsic Euclidean metric invariant of a natural infinite, highly structured family of unsigned graph-edge polytopes. The odd-cycle obstruction changes the associated determinant from ordinary spanning-tree design and produces an exact scalar classification, the entire 3m-vertex contact structure, every semiaxis and volume, and a sharp exponential 3^(-m) approach to a non-obvious quarter-spoke design weight. The precise asymptotic fact is motivated by how the nonbipartite prism geometry allocates covariance over distinct edge orbits; it is not an arbitrary numerical slice.
